title: A mental cause added to a sufficient physical cause is idle

statements.text: Supposing that every mental effect in the physical world also has a sufficient physical cause offends parsimony and fails the leading intuition against epiphenomenalism, that the mental makes a difference. It also means no one could ever need to suppose anything nonphysical at work in neural events or behavior.

sources.quote: This view, however, both offends Occamist principles and fails to satisfy the leading anti-epiphenomenalist intuition
there could never be any reason to introduce mental causes into one’s account of neural events or behavior
